release review · one policy choice

Compare expired-session recovery

The same five-call replay is shown under the current and proposed policies. Each result remains visible while you decide what ships.

current result

Refresh every failed request

Behavior

Each call that receives an expired-session response starts its own credential refresh, then retries once with the returned token.

Five-call replay

/orders    401 → refresh A → retry
/cart      401 → refresh B → retry
/profile   401 → refresh C → retry
/offers    401 → refresh D → retry
/delivery  401 → refresh E → retry
Refresh requests
5
Original calls retried
5
Failure fan-out
Independent

Release consequence

No client behavior changes. A busy tab can still send several refresh requests for one expired credential, and each request can finish with a different refresh result.

proposed result

Share one refresh per tab

Behavior

The first expired-session response starts a refresh. Other calls in that tab wait for it, then retry once with the same returned token.

Five-call replay

/orders   ┐
/cart     │
/profile  ├→ refresh A → retry all five
/offers   │
/delivery ┘
Refresh requests
1
Original calls retried
5
Failure fan-out
Shared

Release consequence

Concurrent calls reuse one refresh result. If that refresh fails, all five calls return the same failure without retrying with a stale token.

Which policy should ship?

Both policies retry each original call once; the choice is whether a tab coordinates the credential refresh behind those retries.

Keep independent refreshes Adopt one shared refresh per tab
